reviewed_proposal_texts.tooltip: While a CPU-heavy job such as Measure runs, this policy caps backdrops that are already animating at no more than 30 fps and pauses Spaceout fractals. While a GPU job such as mask generation runs, decorative rendering uses the CPU and GPU-backed Spaceout fractals pause. Your saved animation settings return when the jobs end. Off disables this workload policy; other animation limits still apply.
reviewed_proposal_texts.stop:
Stop the animation timer and retire the shading thread.

When a shading producer exists and the widget is visible with a
:class:`_BufferedEngine`, retain its last published frame, if available,
as the still drawn by :meth:`_paint_still`. This applies regardless of
why :meth:`stop` was called. A hidden widget does not retain that
published frame. Stopping does not imply that every other piece of
renderer or widget state is released.

A CPU-heavy run does not itself stop a backdrop that otherwise qualifies
to animate: the workload policy and :func:`spacr.qt.gil_priority.active`
can pace it to no more than :data:`_RUN_FPS`. The animation switch,
visibility, Reduce motion and minimization still govern whether it runs.
release_bullets: Field backgrounds on Mask screens and in Spaceout use frame-rate caps of up to 60 fps. Workload pacing can lower the cap for active backdrops to 30 fps. Actual frame rates depend on the display and load. Ripples from a closed window run outward only, and the ripple slider scales waves up to 200 %.
Preferences includes changes intended to reduce delays when opening, applying and closing.
The README is rebuilt from images, and the slide deck is rebuilt to match. README and interface localization catalogs are available in nine languages.
